messages:
jess: :rotating_light: incident-bot did not page the on-call at 14:07 for the customer-prod alert. Alerts landed in #incidents but no pages were sent. Anyone oncall?
kevin: I'm oncall. I didn't get a page. I see two alerts in the channel at 14:06 and 14:07.
incidents-bot: [automated] Alert routed: PROD::payment-timeout -> incident-bot webhook posted (status 200)
jess: weird. logs show the webhook POST returned 200, but incident-bot shows "suppressed by policy" in its internal logs.
infra-bot: posting smallest useful log snippet:
```
2024-06-12T14:06:58Z POST /webhook -> 200
2024-06-12T14:06:58Z incident-bot recv payload id=abc123 sig_header=sha256=deadbeef
2024-06-12T14:06:58Z signature verify failed: header missing key-type
2024-06-12T14:06:58Z action: suppressed
```
sara: that signature error is new, we rolled the webhook signer a week ago but incident-bot should be tolerant. @kevin can you confirm oncall rotation in DB?
kevin: confirmed I'm current oncall until 2024-06-13.
kevin: looking at incident-bot logs now, grep shows a spate of `signature verify failed` messages starting 14:00. Something changed upstream (pagerflow) — headers include `X-Sig-Type:v2` now instead of `v1`.
jess: ah — we shipped the stricter verifier last week that expects `v1` only. Failing that, we mark events as unauthenticated and drop/pause to avoid false pages. That explains suppression.
support-ops: customer-facing impact: two customers reported increased API latency ~14:07 and our SREs didn't get immediate page. We manually paged at 14:12. One customer opened a severity-2 during the gap.
kevin: mitigation plan: 1) temporary rollback the strict verifier (toggle `VERIFY_SIG_STRICT=false`) 2) re-trigger processing for queued webhooks 3) notify customers. I'll do 1 now.
jess: approve. Please post the exact command you run.
kevin: running:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/incident-bot VERIFY_SIG_STRICT=false --record
```
infra-bot: rollout started: incident-bot v2.4.3 -> v2.4.4 (env change).
kevin: rollout completed, new pods healthy. 
incident-bot: [automated] signature mode=permissive; unhandled queue length=12 -> reprocessing
incident-bot: [automated] reprocessed 12 events, paged 2 oncalls: kevin, tim
jess: did pages go out? kevin?
kevin: yes, I got fresh pages at 14:13 for the backlog. Confirmed one subsequent customer S2 escalation got proper paging.
tim: I saw a duplicate page for one alert — looks like reprocessing didn't dedupe properly. Got two SMSes. :grimacing:
jess: noted. we should dedupe by event id.
sara: root cause hypothesis: pagerflow switched sig header to `X-Sig-Type:v2` plus new signing key id. Our verifier rejected unknown `v2`. The stricter verifier was merged to hard-fail unknown types.
kevin: short-term mitigation done. Longer-term fix: update verifier to accept v2 and fallback to legacy sigs + add better logging + make suppression explicit in channel. I'll open a ticket.
jess: assign owner + timeline?
kevin: owner=kevin, PR to accept `v2` by EOD, QA tomorrow AM. Will include dedupe idempotency fix.
support-ops: action for support: we sent notice to affected customers and added incident notes; no PII exposed.
infra-bot: action created: ENG-INC-4321 -> "incident-bot: support v2 sig header and idempotent reprocess" assigned to kevin
jess: TL;DR for postmortem: incident-bot strict verifier rejected new header type and suppressed pages; automation allowed a silent suppression without a loud channel notification; manual pages required. Impact: delayed on-call alerting for ~6 minutes; one customer S2 escalated; duplicate pages during reprocess. Remediation: revert strict mode, support v2 header, dedupe reprocess, surface suppressions to #incidents.
kevin: I'll also add an outbound healthcheck that posts to #incidents every 5m if any webhooks are suppressed > 1min.
tim: can we add a mute window when we reprocess to avoid duplicates? maybe tag reprocessed events so dedupe sees them.
jess: good. Also add runbook steps for manual paging: `scripts/manual-page.sh <oncall>` -> documented in eng-oncall.
kevin: created PR draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/incident-bot/pulls/128 (will add tests for v2)
sara: FYI security/ops: verify signing rotation process; add spec for header versions.
support-ops: customer comms: update sent at 14:45, link to internal notes.
jess: thanks all. we'll keep this thread for actions until postmortem. Follow ups: ENG-INC-4321 (kevin) / postmortem writeup (jess) / runbook update (tim). :white_check_mark: 
kevin: noted, will update ticket with timeline and root cause.
incidents-bot: [automated] thread closed by jess at 15:01 (summary posted)."
